I have no literature-search tool in this session (no PubMed/Europe PMC/web access, no shell), so I could not run a query. What follows is **from my own knowledge**, with a training cutoff of **May 2026** — so it covers work up to roughly early 2026 and will miss anything from the last ~6 months. Citation details (volume/page/DOI) are recalled, not retrieved; treat them as leads to verify rather than verified references. I flag my confidence on each.

## Co-folding models that changed the antibody picture

- **AlphaFold3** — Abramson et al., *Nature* 630:493–500 (2024), doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07487-9. High confidence. Antibody–antigen interfaces were called out explicitly as a weak spot that AF3 improves on relative to AlphaFold-Multimer. The most consequential practical finding: **antibody–antigen accuracy scales strongly with the number of random seeds sampled**, far more than other interface classes — a single seed badly understates achievable accuracy. Weights were released for non-commercial use in November 2024.
- **AlphaFold-Multimer** — Evans et al., bioRxiv 2021, doi:10.1101/2021.10.04.463034. High confidence. Still the baseline most antibody benchmarks compare against.
- **Open AF3-class reimplementations**, all of which handle antibody–antigen inputs: **Boltz-1** (Wohlwend et al., bioRxiv, Nov 2024), **Boltz-2** (2025, adds binding-affinity prediction), **Chai-1** (Chai Discovery, Sept 2024), **Protenix** (ByteDance, 2025), **OpenFold3** (2025). High confidence these exist and are antibody-capable; moderate confidence on exact release months.

## Antibody-specific structure predictors

- **IgFold** — Ruffolo, Chu, Mahajan & Gray, *Nature Communications* 14:2389 (2023). High confidence. Built on the AntiBERTy language model; near-AF2 accuracy at roughly a second per structure.
- **ImmuneBuilder** (ABodyBuilder2, NanoBodyBuilder2, TCRBuilder2) — Abanades et al., *Communications Biology* 6:575 (2023). High confidence.
- **ABodyBuilder3** — Kenlay et al., *Bioinformatics* (2024). Moderate-to-high confidence; adds language-model embeddings and pLDDT-style per-residue error estimates, with better CDR-H3 handling.
- **ABlooper** — Abanades et al., *Bioinformatics* 38:1877 (2022), CDR loop prediction with an equivariant GNN. High confidence on the work, moderate on pagination.
- **tFold-Ab / tFold** (Tencent) — fast antibody and antibody–antigen modeling without MSAs; bioRxiv 2024 with a journal version I can't pin down. Moderate confidence.
- **NanoNet** and nanobody-focused evaluations — high confidence the subfield exists; I'd verify specific recent nanobody benchmarks before citing.

## Benchmarks and critical evaluations (the most useful reading)

- **Yin & Pierce**, "Evaluation of AlphaFold antibody–antigen modeling with implications for improving predictive accuracy," *Protein Science* 33:e4865 (2024). Moderate-to-high confidence. This group's earlier paper — Yin, Feng, Varshney & Pierce, *Protein Science* 31:e4379 (2022) — established that antibody–antigen complexes are a distinct failure mode for AF2, not just generically hard complexes.
- **SAbDab** (Dunbar et al., *NAR* 2014, continuously updated) is the standard source of structures for these benchmarks, and date-based splits against it are how most of these papers avoid train/test leakage. High confidence.
- There were AF3-era antibody–antigen benchmark papers appearing through 2025, but I cannot name specific titles or venues with confidence and will not guess.

## Design-adjacent work, since it's usually what people want next

- **RFantibody / RFdiffusion for antibodies** — Bennett et al. (Baker lab), epitope-specific de novo antibody and VHH design; bioRxiv 2024, code released early 2025, with a journal version I believe appeared in 2025. Moderate confidence on the publication status, high on the work's existence.
- **Chai-2** — technical report (2025) claiming double-digit experimental hit rates for zero-shot de novo antibody design. Moderate confidence; this was a company report, not peer-reviewed, when I last saw it.
- **AntiFold** — antibody-specific inverse folding (Høie et al.). Moderate confidence on venue and year.

## The consensus state of the field, as of my cutoff

1. **Framework and canonical CDRs are effectively solved** — sub-angstrom to ~1 Å RMSD from any modern method, including the fast antibody-specific ones.
2. **CDR-H3 remains the bottleneck**, typically ~2–3 Å RMSD, and pLDDT/predicted-error is only a partial guide there.
3. **Antibody–antigen complex prediction is still the open problem.** It lags general protein–protein complex prediction substantially, almost certainly because antibody paratope–epitope recognition is not encoded in co-evolutionary signal the way obligate complexes are. Practical mitigation in the AF3 era is heavy seed sampling plus ranking, and epitope restraints when you have them.
4. **Affinity and the effect of point mutations are not predicted reliably** by structure-prediction accuracy. Boltz-2's affinity head is the notable attempt to address this directly.

Caveat worth stating plainly: I could not verify any of the above against a live index, and I may be wrong on a journal, year, or whether a preprint has since been published. I'd confirm each on PubMed or Europe PMC before citing. If you can give me a PubMed/Europe PMC tool in a later session, I can run a proper dated search (e.g. `("AlphaFold"[tiab]) AND (antibody[tiab] OR nanobody[tiab]) AND structure prediction`) and return a real, current result set with PMIDs.

## ANSWER

I could not search the literature — no literature/web tool exists in this session — so this is recalled knowledge with a **May 2026 cutoff** and unverified citation details.

Key recent work on AlphaFold + antibody structure prediction:
- **AlphaFold3** — Abramson et al., *Nature* 630:493–500 (2024); improves antibody–antigen interfaces, with accuracy scaling strongly with number of seeds.
- **Open AF3-class co-folding models**: Boltz-1/Boltz-2, Chai-1, Protenix, OpenFold3 (2024–2025); Boltz-2 adds affinity prediction.
- **Antibody-specific predictors**: IgFold (*Nat Commun* 14:2389, 2023), ImmuneBuilder (*Commun Biol* 6:575, 2023), ABodyBuilder3 (*Bioinformatics* 2024), ABlooper (*Bioinformatics* 2022), tFold-Ab (2024).
- **Critical benchmarks**: Yin & Pierce, *Protein Science* 33:e4865 (2024) and 31:e4379 (2022), using SAbDab date-split sets.
- **Design-adjacent**: RFantibody/RFdiffusion antibody design (Bennett et al., 2024–2025), Chai-2 report (2025), AntiFold.

State of the field: framework/canonical CDRs essentially solved (~1 Å); **CDR-H3 still ~2–3 Å**; **antibody–antigen complex prediction remains the major unsolved problem**, well behind general complex prediction; affinity prediction not reliable from structure accuracy alone.
